newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden commission to say No to EMU - newspaper. [CORRECTED 09:01 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sweden commission to say No to EMU - newspaper. [CORRECTED 09:01 GMT]

text.p: A Swedish government commission investigating whether Sweden should join the EU's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) will recommend that Sweden does not join, a Swedish daily said on Thursday.

The daily Dagens Politik (corrects from Dagens Nyheter), quoting sources with access to the commission's findings, said it would recommend rejection of EMU membership when it announces its findings next Monday.

The commission, led by Professor Lars Calmfors, was set up by the Swedish government to examine the consequences for Sweden of Swedish EMU membership and its findings are expected to play an important role in Sweden's decision on EMU.

Dagens Politik said the commission had been unable to find any valid economic arguments for Swedish EMU membership and that it had concluded the proposed European currency, the Euro, risked being unstable and weak.

"Joint monetary and currency policies are necessary for those who want a more tightly knit union in Europe, but the case for EMU collapses without that desire for closer union," the daily quoted the report as saying.

The commission's report, seen as a crucial part of Prime Minister Goran Persson's decision-making process on Swedish EMU-membership, would say membership could eventually lead to a federation of member states.
Sweden's ability to take independent economic measures to stimulate its economy would also be curtailed, the daily quoted the report as saying.
